item.title: SpaceX Q3 revenue soars 161% YoY on AI business growth, beating estimates
item.description: Elon Musk's SpaceX on Tuesday reported a 161% rise in revenue for the third quarter, beating estimates, buoyed by a surge in its AI business and steady growth at its Starlink
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: Elon Musk’s SpaceX registered a 161% year-on-year surge in third-quarter revenue, beating analyst estimates, driven by a surge in its artificial intelligence business and steady growth in its Starlink satellite-internet unit, Reuters reported.Revenue rose to $14.6 billion in the quarter, well above analysts’ estimate of $12.72 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.Starlink and SpaceX’s broader connectivity operations remain the company’s primary revenue drivers, helping fund CEO Musk’s AI ambitions. However, SpaceX’s AI software offerings, including xAI’s Grok, have yet to match the traction of rivals such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google.For live updates on US Markets, click hereSpaceX generates most of its AI revenue by leasing data-centre computing capacity to developers, including Anthropic, Google and Reflection AI, rather than relying on its own AI models. This makes the business more akin to a cloud-computing provider than a traditional AI developer.Its AI operations span Grok, the social-media platform X and an expanding data-centre business, which has also become the company's largest investment area. Revenue comes from computing contracts with Anthropic, Google, owned by Alphabet, and Reflection AI.However, the AI division continues to incur substantial operating losses. SpaceX has warned that significant, sustained spending will be necessary before the business can achieve consistent profitability.Meanwhile, Starlink continues to add subscribers, supported by further satellite launches and an expanding portfolio of services for consumers, businesses, airlines, maritime operators and government agencies.SpaceX has warned that expanding into markets beyond wealthier countries could bring down its average revenue per user over time. Investors are monitoring whether this pressure is beginning to emerge as the company enters more international markets and introduces cheaper subscription plans.Another key concern is whether SpaceX can sustain its growth while improving network profitability. The company continues to invest heavily in expanding coverage, increasing capacity and developing direct-to-device mobile connectivity services.Meanwhile, Starship, SpaceX’s next-generation reusable rocket system, has yet to begin commercial operations. The vehicle is expected to help deploy more advanced, higher-bandwidth Starlink satellites and support AI-computing infrastructure in orbit. Achieving reliable, repeated reuse of Starship remains a crucial part of SpaceX’s long-term strategy.SpaceX deployed several Starlink satellites last month during Starship’s first orbital test flight, which ended earlier than planned following an engine problem.The company’s space operations cover commercial launches, government missions and the development of Starship, making the segment a major source of expenditure and uncertainty. While Falcon rocket launches have remained strong, revenue fluctuates depending on the balance between internal Starlink deployments, commercial launches and government contracts.SpaceX has increasingly prioritised launches for its own satellite network over missions carrying third-party payloads, while continuing to shoulder substantial costs associated with Starship’s development.Investors will also be watching for comments from CEO Elon Musk on a potential merger between SpaceX and Tesla, a widely discussed possibility. Tesla is scheduled to report its results on Wednesday.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

item.title: Copper stays range bound as US tariff uncertainty, oil inflation risks weigh
item.description: Copper prices remained range bound as uncertainty over potential US tariffs and inflation risks from higher oil prices kept traders cautious. China’s copper scrap shortage supported refined copper demand, while record high US inventories and cautious buying limited gains. Goldman Sachs expects copper prices to average $15,400 a ton in 2027.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: Copper prices remained stuck in a narrow range on Tuesday, with uncertainty over potential US import tariffs and concerns that higher oil prices could fuel inflation keeping traders cautious, Reuters reported.Three month copper on the London Metal Exchange was up 0.1% at $14,353 a metric ton by 0955 GMT, marking a third straight session of tight trading.The metal has gained 55% since Donald Trump returned to the US presidency in January 2025, even as global demand fell 0.5% to 27 million metric tons, Panmure Liberum analyst Tom Price said in a note.China demand offers supportA shortage of copper scrap in China was providing another source of support. Goldman Sachs said the shortfall was increasing China's need for refined copper through domestic inventory drawdowns, while the US continued importing metal and building stocks ahead of possible tariffs.The Yangshan copper premium, a key gauge of China's demand for imported copper, climbed 0.7% to $138 a ton, its highest level in almost four years.Tariff uncertainty keeps traders cautiousThe White House is yet to decide on tariffs on refined copper, with the administration increasingly focused on affordability ahead of November's midterm elections, Reuters reported in September, citing people familiar with the matter.Chinese broker Everbright Futures said cautious purchasing at high prices and uncertainty over US tariffs could keep copper prices range bound in the near term.Meanwhile, copper inventories on the Comex stood at a record 718,199 metric tons, up sharply from 87,241 in January 2025, highlighting the build up of metal in the US.Goldman Sachs expects copper prices to average $15,400 in 2027, compared with $14,700 at the end of 2026.Supply disruptions also remained in focus. BHP Group and Anglo American reported copper production declines of 19% and 5%, respectively, due to disruptions in Chile, although both maintained their full year output guidance.Among other LME metals, aluminium fell 0.8% to $2,993, zinc lost 0.7% to $3,688, while nickel rose 0.5% to $15,600. Tin gained 0.1% and lead was steady. (Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

item.title: US stocks today: US stocks gain as healthcare stocks hit record high, oil prices fall
item.description: Wall Street's main indexes saw increases driven by a rally in healthcare stocks that reached record highs. Easing oil prices contributed to a recovery from the previous week's technology led selloff. Major companies like General Motors and Steel Dynamics reported disappointing earnings forecasts, while 3M and Equifax exceeded expectations. Investors are closely monitoring upcoming corporate earnings reports from several high-profile companies.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: Wall Street's main indexes climbed on Tuesday as healthcare stocks rallied to record highs and easing oil prices helped extend a recovery from last week's technology led selloff, according to Reuters.The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.22%, while the S&P 500 gained 0.70% and the Nasdaq Composite added 0.59%. Healthcare and financial stocks led gains in the S&P 500, rising 1.8% and 1%, respectively, while energy stocks lagged.Brent crude fell 1.3% after briefly touching a near five month high, adding to the positive mood across broader markets, Reuters reported.Healthcare stocks lead reboundHealthcare stocks led the rebound, with S&P 500 Healthcare index rising 2.28% and hitting a record high. Eli Lilly rose 5.56% to $1,309 while United Health was up3.19% at $419.79.The gains came a day after the S&P 500 and Nasdaq extended their rebound as investors returned to technology stocks following last week's sharp selloff, which was partly driven by concerns over CoreWeave's debt load and the cost of financing the AI buildout, Reuters said.AI linked stocks were mixed on Tuesday. CoreWeave gained 1.6%, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor index rose 0.4%. You're seeing some strength in some high value stocks and the Dow, and so that's helping to sort of lift the overall index, said Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth, according to Reuters. Concerns about what's going on as far as semiconductors, that's still there and AI related names are down, but for the most part, the rest of the market is seeing a bit of a nice rebound. Earnings take centre stageInvestors were also looking to this week's corporate earnings for signs of whether companies can sustain growth amid mounting macroeconomic risks, Reuters reported.General Motors shares fell 5.3% after its full year earnings forecast came in below analysts' expectations. Steel Dynamics declined 1% after missing third quarter profit estimates.On the other hand, 3M jumped 5.3% after expanding its data centre partnership with Amazon and raising its full year profit forecast. Equifax gained 9.6% after reporting third quarter profit above analysts' estimates.The earnings calendar remained busy, with SpaceX and Netflix due to report after Tuesday's close, followed by Meta Platforms and Tesla on Wednesday.Meanwhile, South Korean AI infrastructure company Elice Group tumbled nearly 30% in its market debut, falling below its IPO price.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

item.title: US Stocks: GE Aerospace raises 2026 profit forecast as services strength drives growth
item.description: GE Aerospace has increased its 2026 adjusted earnings forecast due to continued demand for engine maintenance. The demand for spare parts remains high, which supports their financial outlook. Airlines are facing rising fuel costs due to disruptions in oil supply and are adjusting their capacity accordingly. Despite potential pressures on flight schedules, GE Aerospace's revenue from services is expected to remain strong.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: GE Aerospace on Tuesday raised its 2026 profit forecast for the second time this year, betting strong demand for engine maintenance and spare parts will offset the impact of higher fuel costs on flights.Airlines worldwide are cutting costs and capacity to defend ticket prices after the war in Iran disrupted oil shipping routes, driving up jet fuel costs and adding to pressure on the industry.With no end to the war in sight, higher fuel prices are testing airlines' ability to maintain schedules and margins, raising the risk of fewer flights and weaker demand for maintenance.GE Aerospace has said, however, that any impact on services revenue and profit this year should be limited, as much of its 2026 engine shop-visit work is already under contract and demand for spare parts continues to outstrip supply.Last month, GE Aerospace finance chief Rahul Ghai said the company had seen no changes to airlines' fleet plans, while the number of parked aircraft remained low.The jet-engine maker now expects 2026 adjusted earnings of $8.00 to $8.10 per share, up from its prior forecast of $7.65 to $7.85, and above analysts' consensus estimate of $7.92, according to data compiled by LSEG. We are raising our 2026 guidance across the board, and we now expect 2027 commercial services to grow low-double-digits supported by our over $170 billion commercial services backlog, CEO Larry Culp said in a statement.Through CFM International, its joint venture with France's Safran, GE Aerospace is a leading supplier of engines for narrowbody jets and a major player in the widebody market. Parts and services account for more than 70% of its commercial engine revenue.Quarterly revenue at its commercial engines and services unit climbed 21% to $10.34 billion, driven by strong demand for aftermarket services. The company also raised its 2026 revenue growth forecast for the segment to the low 20% range, compared with its previous expectation of about 20% growth.It reported an adjusted profit of $2.25 per share for the quarter through September, beating Wall Street expectations of $2.01.Shares of the company rose nearly 1.2% in premarket trading.

item.title: US Stocks: GM's core profit rises 22% on strength of pickup-truck business
item.description: General Motors exceeded analyst expectations in third-quarter earnings, driven by robust demand for their pickups and SUVs. The company reported an adjusted EBIT of $4.1 billion, marking a 22% year-over-year increase. Despite facing inflationary challenges, GM forecasts an adjusted EBIT of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion by 2026. Additionally, a $20 billion stock buyback program was initiated to bolster share value.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: General Motors' third-quarter results easily beat analyst expectations on the back of resolute shoppers who continue to spring for pricey pickups and SUVs.The company on Tuesday said quarterly earnings before interest and tax, not including one-time items (adjusted EBIT) rose 22% from a year earlier, to $4.1 billion. That amounted to $3.70 per share, topping analyst expectations of $3.63, according to LSEG data.The automaker said it expected to end 2026 with adjusted EBIT in the range of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion, narrowed from previous guidance of $14 billion to $16 billion. The company said it remained confident despite inflationary pressures from higher logistics and energy costs, tariffs and other expenses.GM shares fell about 6% in premarket trading.The company said its board approved a multi-year, $20 billion stock buyback program. GM has bought back about $29.5 billion of its own shares since 2023, driving down its overall share count to help its per-share profit results.GM in the third quarter sold a higher mix of large pickup trucks and fewer electric vehicles, which helped the bottom line. The automaker has been pulling back on sales of EVs, which historically have lost money, following the Trump administration's withdrawal of support for them.Revenue totaled $50 billion, up 2.9% from a year earlier. In North America, the company's profit margin improved to 8.7%, from 6.2% a year earlier, despite a slight decline in quarterly sales.GM said the path forward is more challenging, but reiterated that it expects next year's results to be better, assuming continued strong consumer demand and a moderating of cost pressures on commodities and logistics.
